I'd like to say right up front that I like paper books too and by no means should we stop buying them. I'm an early adopter technophile, so I wanted one. I had the first gen kindle with the physical buttons and loved it. I broke it because I carried it everywhere and got careless. My next purchase was the first model cheapo sponsored kindle I bought used off a sleazy coworker. He overcharged me and it was defective (non-existent battery life), but I still ran it for almost two years. I didn't like the functionality of the touchscreen; I wanted another push button model.
I got the current gen base model paperwhite this past year, with the slightly larger screen, and I couldn't be happier with it. At first I was leery of the back-lighting, I'd heard pros and cons on that issue. But after a quick adjustment to suit my tastes, it doesn't effect the experience at all. I have found it very convenient and relaxing to read in bed and elsewhere without a light on, and I have experienced zero eyestrain. I can't stand extended reading on LCD screens because the lighting is unnatural for me. The kindle is not like that. The touchscreen has come along since the first edition. The screen on my previous kindle was overly sensitive.It would flip a page at the lightest contact and had a tendency to skip many pages ahead on accident. It was probably some unintentional gesture on my part, but still, too sensitive. In fairness I probably could have figured it out by googling it, but I always intended to replace it soon so didn't bother. The touchscreen on my current kindle seems to strike a good balance between responsiveness and stability. I can lay it face down on a bed spread or walk away from it with cats in the area and not come back to find it skipped many chapters ahead, with spoilers lurking before my unsuspecting eyes. Because of the aforementioned screen sensitivity, and because battery life on previous second kindle sucked, I developed the habit of shutting down every time I paused to get up or move to another reading location. The battery life on my newest kindle is great and I rarely even think about it nowadays. I plug it in about once a week for a few hours when it occurs to me I haven't charged it in a while. I do still shutdown every night or when I'm done reading for a while just out of habit though. As you can tell I like kindle, but I think that also comes from a voracious appetite for books. I'm no kindle expert, but I could go on with other good things about owning one. If anyone is interested in hearing more, I'd be glad to add more to the discussion.

I think @vercingetorix wasn't meaning just the store, but also the format that the books are distributed in. You can't take the books you purchase for instance, and read them on another device in the future. That way, Amazon has you locked into their ecosystem if you want to continue using those books. It's bad for consumers as it punishes you with your purchases for moving on to a Sony eReader, Kobo, etc. It is possible to remove the DRM with a library organizer like Calibre for those inclined to do so.
